chunks: We were told by my father, may Allah grant him mercy, that he said: We were told by Sa’d bin Abdullah, from Ya’qoub bin Yazid, from Muhammed ibn Abi ‘Umayr, from some of his companions, from Abu Abdillah, peace be upon him, that he said:
The kalala is when there is no parent nor child (to someone).

key_terms.الْكَلَالَةُ: Kalala: A person who dies without a parent or child as an heir

ai.seo_question: What is the definition of Kalala in Shia inheritance jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This hadith from Shaykh al-Saduq’s *Ma'ani al-Akhbar* offers the foundational definition of 'al-kalala' as a deceased person lacking both direct ascendants (parents) and descendants (children). In Shia jurisprudence, this definition is critical for determining the distribution of the residual estate to collateral relatives, such as siblings, when the primary lines of inheritance are absent. It clarifies the scope of the term as used in the Quranic verse of inheritance, ensuring precise application of shares among extended family members.
